cost_disclaimer: Every ph/lab/cap figure is a [C] estimate unless the note says otherwise. They are calibrated so that the SHAPE of the tree is right: which items are cheap, which are slow, which are gated on people rather than money. Do not read three significant figures into any of them.

goals.blurb: Reach the junction device that made the electronic age practical.
goals.name: Grown and alloy junction transistors

goals.blurb: Found the method itself: controlled experiment, hypothesis, and a result someone else can repeat.
goals.name: Establish experimental science

goals.blurb: Show, not just argue, that disease has a cause you can see and name.
goals.name: Develop germ theory

goals.blurb: Write down everything you know, plainly enough that it outlives you.
goals.name: Leave behind a written corpus

goals.blurb: Rise from a curiosity the state tolerates to someone it funds and defends.
goals.name: Win the patronage of the state

goals.blurb: Build the first source of a steady electric current.
goals.name: Establish electrical generation

goals.blurb: Found the schools that make reading common rather than rare, and see it show up in the census.
goals.name: Raise literacy above a fifth

goals.blurb: Cut most of what plague and famine take, with sanitation, quarantine and the vaccines germ theory makes possible.
goals.name: Curb epidemic mortality

goals.blurb: Build the first engine that turns heat into work without a river or a draft animal.
goals.name: Produce a steam engine

goals.blurb: Make parts to a tolerance where any one of them fits in place of any other.
goals.name: Interchangeable manufacturing

goals.blurb: Field the all-big-gun steel battleship that makes every earlier navy obsolete.
goals.name: Build a modern navy

goals.blurb: Carry a signal the distance a continent, or an ocean, actually needs.
goals.name: Span a continent by telegraph

goals.blurb: Move from a blacksmith's iron to a steel industry: bulk production, alloys, and steel that does not rust.
goals.name: Industrialise steel

goals.blurb: Turn the radio from a signalling device into a medium: scheduled programming, an audience, a business.
goals.name: Radio broadcasting

goals.blurb: Pull nitrogen from the air itself and put it on the fields, ending the old ceiling on how much food the land can give.
goals.name: Synthetic fertiliser

goals.blurb: Build a heavier-than-air machine that takes off, flies under its own power, and lands under control.
goals.name: Powered flight

goals.blurb: Mechanise the fields enough to free the children working them, and put nearly everyone who could read before you in a classroom.
goals.name: Maximise literacy

schema.art: minimum trained technical artisans required on staff to attempt
schema.bounty_rule: A node can be bought as a public prize when its craft category is glass_optics, metallurgy, precision, power, agriculture, information, or instruments, or when the selected civilization has a strong local craft tradition. The test is whether a local artisan could recognise success without understanding the theory. Price is c. 2.5x honest cost, costs the poster no hours of their own, consumes no supervision slot. See 04_ECONOMICS.md section 7.
schema.cap: one-off capital in denarii beyond labour and materials (land, buildings, purchased tools)
schema.conf: A well attested, B probable, C author's estimate
schema.gov: State interest, -3 (will actively suppress) to +3 (will fund and demand). NEGATIVE VALUES ARE ENFORCED BY THE SIMULATOR: a node with gov < 0 costs 25% more per point (bribes, delay, relocation to a province, a compliant front man), adds 3 extra suspicion per point, cannot be attempted without at least a local patron, and at gov <= -2 requires senatorial patronage. This is the 'you need social approval for this' mechanic.
schema.kb: knowledge file and anchor holding the actual how-to
schema.lab: hired labour hours by trade; priced from data/prices.json wage_rates
schema.mat: materials consumed, key = item in prices.json, value = kg or units
schema.name: human name
schema.note: commentary, warnings, and reasoning for the numbers
schema.ph: YOUR OWN hours. The scarcest resource in the game. c. 2400/yr available.
schema.pre: list of prerequisite node ids (AND semantics)
schema.rev: net revenue in denarii per year at maturity, 0 if not a product
schema.risk: probability a given attempt fails outright and must be retried at 40% of cost
schema.sch: minimum trained natural philosophers required on staff to attempt
schema.up: annual upkeep in denarii once operating
schema.yrs: minimum calendar years, a floor that labour cannot buy down (curing, growing, seasoning, maturation)
